newsitem.title: GERMANY: Asiana Airlines expects strong '97 growth.
newsitem.headline: Asiana Airlines expects strong '97 growth.

text.p: Korean carrier Asiana Airlines said it would show strong double-figure growth in both international passenger and cargo business in 1997.
The private airline, owned by Korean transport and manufacturing conglomerate, the Kumho Group, expected to increase international passenger numbers 21 percent to 3.48 million this year.
International passenger sales revenue should rise 31 percent to 875.5 million dollars, a company statement said.
International air cargo tonnage was expected to grow 25 percent to 298,299 tonnes in 1997 and cargo sales revenue should rise 24 percent to 419.3 million dollars.

Asiana, launched eight years ago as a rival to Korean Air Lines, said it aimed to double its current air cargo tonnage and sales revenue by the year 2000 to get into the top ten of world air cargo carriers.

The airline would bring 21 new aircraft into service within the next three years and double its fleet to 100 aircraft by 2005 from its current 49 Boeing 747, 767 and 737 aircraft, the statement added.

Asiana currently operates 185 international flights a week to 40 destinations in 19 countries, mostly to Japan, the U.S. and south-east Asia, and also 633 weekly domestic flights. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
